chapters.title: 1. Pair Sum in a Sorted List

paras.t: Pair Sum in a Sorted List.
You get a list of integers nums sorted from smallest to largest, and a number target. Find the two different positions whose values add up to target and return them as [i, j] with i < j.
paras.s: You get a list of integers nums sorted from smallest to largest, and a number target. Find the two different positions whose values add up to target and return them as i, j with i is less than j.

paras.t: Put one pointer, L, on the smallest number and another, R, on the largest.
If their sum is too small, the only way to grow it is to move L to the right. If it is too big, move R to the left. Each step throws away one number that can never be part of the answer.
Time O(n), space O(1). Each step moves one pointer inward, so we take at most n steps and only store two indexes.
paras.s: Time O of n, space O of one. Each step moves one pointer inward, so we take at most n steps and only store two indexes.

paras.t: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list so the last node becomes the first, and return the new head.
Use two pointers: prev starts empty and cur starts at the head.
At each node, remember the next node, flip cur.next to point back at prev, then slide both pointers one step forward. When cur falls off the end, prev is the new head.

paras.s: Time O of n, space O of one.

paras.t: Given a string s, return the length of the longest contiguous piece of s in which no character appears twice.
Keep a window from L to R that never contains a repeat, and remember the last index where each character was seen.
When the new character at R was already seen inside the window, jump L just past that earlier copy. The window is valid again, so we update the best length.
Time O(n), space O(k). R visits every character once and L only moves forward, so the work is linear. The map holds at most one entry per distinct character, k.
paras.s: Time O of n, space O of k. R visits every character once and L only moves forward, so the work is linear. The map holds at most one entry per distinct character, k.
